Both disclosures emphasize the integration of AI capabilities (AIOps for AVGO, Ryzen AI/NPUs for AMD) as a key driver for improving the customer experience and business outcomes in their respective markets.

comparisons.peer_topic: PC Market AI Capabilities and Client SSD Portfolio Expansion
comparisons.peer_summary: Next-generation PCs require higher performance SSDs due to AI capabilities; SBU expanded its portfolio in 2024 with the 3500 NVMe SSD built on Micron G8 NAND, targeting demanding business and consumer workloads.
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and MU discuss the impact of AI on the end-user device market and the resulting requirement for higher performance capabilities, albeit at different layers of the stack. AVGO describes its software products (ValueOps, DevOps, AIOps) as delivering end-to-end visibility to help customers realize better business outcomes and experiences across the digital lifecycle. MU describes the hardware side of this trend, noting that next-generation PCs contain high-performance neural processing chipsets and AI capabilities, which necessitate higher performance SSDs like the 3500 NVMe to handle demanding workloads. Both disclosures link the rise of AI to an increased demand for robust, high-performance computing resources to support better user and business experiences.

comparisons.peer_topic: Automotive Platform Solutions and DRIVE Hyperion Brand
comparisons.peer_summary: The company delivers a complete end-to-end automated driving and in-vehicle cockpit computing solution for the AV market under the DRIVE Hyperion brand, leveraging AI technology leadership and long-standing automotive relationships. The DRIVE Hyperion platform includes high-performance hardware, a reference sensor set, and an open, modular software platform for autonomous driving and intelligent in-vehicle experiences.
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and NVDA emphasize a comprehensive, end-to-end approach to their respective solutions to enhance customer experiences. AVGO structures its products in ValueOps, DevOps, and AIOps domains to deliver end-to-end visibility across the digital lifecycle, aiming for better business outcomes. NVDA similarly markets its Automotive solutions as a complete end-to-end automated driving and in-vehicle cockpit computing solution under the DRIVE Hyperion brand, leveraging AI to deliver intelligent in-vehicle experiences. Both disclosures highlight an integrated platform strategy (software lifecycle for AVGO, hardware/software for automotive for NVDA) designed to improve the overall experience for their customers.

comparisons.peer_topic: AI research focus and on-device capabilities
comparisons.peer_summary: The company conducts broad research and development across AI, including generative AI, with the goal of advancing core capabilities to run on-device and scaling them across industries, leveraging over a decade of investments focused on power efficiency and personalization.
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and QCOM identify AI as a core driver for enhancing user and business experiences through their respective technologies. AVGO organizes its products into AIOps domains to help customers realize better business outcomes and experiences. QCOM focuses its research and development on advancing AI core capabilities to run on-device, aiming to make AI seamless across everyday experiences and power efficiency. While AVGO applies AI at the software/operations level for business outcomes, QCOM applies AI at the hardware/on-device level for consumer and industrial experiences, both sharing the theme of AI-driven improvement in end-user outcomes.

sentences.text: Our products, organized in the domains of ValueOps, DevOps, and AIOps, deliver end-to-end visibility across all stages of the digital lifecycle and help our customers realize better business outcomes and better experiences for their customers.
